questions.q: What does branching allow a DAG to do?
options: Decide, at run time, which of several downstream paths should actually execute
Run every possible task path simultaneously, always
Permanently delete tasks that aren't needed
Skip the scheduler entirely
questions.explain: Branching lets a task choose which downstream path(s) run, deliberately skipping the rest.

options: The task ID (or list of task IDs) that should actually run downstream
A boolean indicating success or failure
The DAG's schedule interval
A log message to display in the UI
questions.explain: The function's return value tells Airflow exactly which downstream task(s) to execute; everything else on that branch is skipped.

questions.q: What does 'Skipped' mean for a task on the unchosen branch?
options: The task was deliberately not run because branching chose a different path — it's not a failure
The task crashed with an error
The task is still queued and will run eventually
The task was deleted from the DAG
questions.explain: Skipped is a correct, intentional state — Airflow recording that this path wasn't meant to run on this particular DAG Run.

questions.q: Why might a 'join' task downstream of a branch get skipped, even when the chosen branch succeeded?
options: By default, a task only runs once ALL upstream tasks succeed — and a skipped (not succeeded) branch fails that condition
Join tasks always fail regardless of upstream state
Airflow randomly skips convergence tasks
This never actually happens in Airflow
questions.explain: The default trigger rule requires all upstream tasks to succeed; a skipped upstream branch doesn't count as succeeded, so the join task is skipped too.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what actually fixes the 'join gets skipped' problem?
options: Trigger Rules, covered in the next lesson
Removing the join task entirely
Always running both branches regardless of the condition
There is no fix — it's expected and unavoidable
questions.explain: Trigger rules let you change the default 'all upstream must succeed' behavior, which is exactly the next lesson's topic.
